gaps: P0: only a bishop portrait (#1); P5: only hazy high-altitude Mittelholzer aerials (1930–31) where the city is a gray blur
notes: Braun and Hogenberg plate (vol. 3, 1581; #2–#5) not used: Grenoble fills only 38% of the plate width (shared with Romans) and is a perspective plan. #11 is from Topographia Galliae (issued 1655–61), so ‘about 1660’; the BnF record only says 17th century. #8 is Canaletto’s Venice and #20 Detaille’s Champigny panorama fragment (Grenoble museum). #18 Jongkind 1884 is inscribed as a copy after Dagnan’s 1830 painting. #16 lithograph by Charles Motte (died 1836) is misdated 1850.
